thought.text:
## Diagnosis

The error-recovery path in `parse_binding` (parser.py:169-176) calls `reader.read_regex(_rest_of_line)`, where `_rest_of_line = r"[^
]*(?:|
|
)?"`. On CRLF input, the alternation `|
|
` matches `` first, leaving the `
` unconsumed. So the invalid binding's `original.string` ends at ``, and the next binding starts at `
`, giving it `line=2` but `original.string` beginning with `
` rather than `GOOD=ok
`.

## Change Plan

Reorder the alternation to `(?:
|
|)?` so CRLF is consumed as one unit (matching `_newline`/`_end_of_line`). This preserves LF and lone-CR behavior and repeated invalid lines, since each recovery still consumes exactly one line terminator. No other files need changes.
